subject: Discovery recap & onboarding checklist — RetailCo PoC scope
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Jessica Park <jessica.park@retailco.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 11 May 2025 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap & onboarding checklist — RetailCo PoC scope

Hi Jessica / Tom —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap of what we heard and the proposed next steps so the team has a single reference: 

Pain points / goals (as stated)
- Current generation endpoints are inconsistent in latency (avg 600–900ms) during peak business hours; affects checkout personalization throughput.
- Cost per 1k requests is currently too high for experimentation across 50K daily sessions; looking to get to a predictable cost envelope for PoC.
- Need a secure, auditable inference path (SSO + audit logs) for compliance.

Current stack and constraints
- Backend: Node/TypeScript microservices on AWS (ECS Fargate).
- Model usage: transformer-based reranker + in-house prompt template; size ~13B.
- Security: strict VPC peering preferred; SSO (Okta) required for console access.

Success criteria for a 6-week PoC
1) Achieve 2–3x lower median latency under representative load (50 RPS peak).
2) Maintain equivalent or better ranking quality (A/B against current model; metric: NDCG@10).
3) Demonstrate stable per-token cost within agreed threshold ($X / 1k tokens).
4) Deliver an onboarding runbook and auditing snapshots for compliance review.

Proposed PoC scope & milestones (timeline below assumes kickoff next week)
- Week 0: Kickoff + access provisioning (SSO, VPC details, sample dataset) — owners: RetailCo (Jessica/Tom) + Redwood (Monica).
- Week 1–2: Integration & SDK test harness (Node SDK + sample API) — owner: Karthik.
- Week 3: Load testing and latency optimization (batching/kv caching config) — owner: Vivek.
- Week 4: Quality verification (A/B tests on held-out set) — owner: RetailCo + Redwood Research.
- Week 5–6: Wrap-up, cost analysis, and exec readout.

Action items (owners & asks)
- RetailCo (Jessica): Share a 24-hour sample of traffic patterns (anonymized) + Okta admin contact for SSO. Deadline: 2025-05-14.
- Karthik: Send Node SDK example and integration checklist. (attached: integration_checklist.xlsx, sample_api_snippet.py)
- Monica: Draft mutual action plan and PoC acceptance criteria doc (attached).
- Vivek: Confirm target instance sizing and expected concurrency baseline by 2025-05-13.

Attachments: RetailCo_mutual_action_plan.pdf, integration_checklist.xlsx, sample_api_snippet.py (small code sample + curl examples).

I’ve attached a short mutual action plan and an integration checklist to speed the kickoff. If this aligns with what you heard, I propose we lock the kickoff for Tuesday 2025-05-13 at 10:00 AM PT.

Thanks again — excited to partner on this.

Best,
Karthik
Karthik Iyer

Hi Jessica / Tom —

Great — thanks for the quick confirmation and for introducing Sarah on the other thread. To answer your NDCG/export question: yes, the PoC includes a lightweight prediction export hook. Implementation notes below: 

Prediction export options (pick one)
1) Push to S3: Redwood runtime will emit a JSONL of request/response pairs to an S3 bucket you own. We can include request id, input, model response, model_variant, timestamp.
2) Webhook: we can POST each prediction to a customer-provided endpoint (signed webhook).
3) Batch dump: post-run batch export at end of day (for lower-volume samples).

For the Node SDK integration (what Karthik will share), you should expect a simple call pattern: initialize client with API key + optional VPC/region, call generate()/chat()/embed(), and an optional export hook. Example attached (sample_api_snippet.py) — we also have a TypeScript sample in the Drive link if you prefer.

Security & access checklist (what we need from RetailCo)
- Okta SAML metadata (for console access) — owner: Sarah Liu.
- VPC peering CIDR and admin contact for peering setup — owner: Tom.
- IP allowlist for test agents (if you want to restrict).

I’ll convert the mutual action plan to a shared Google Doc for collaborative edits after kickoff. Karthik — I’ll take the lead on coordinating the infra access work and will post a short onboarding runbook to the Drive link by EOD today.

Thanks,
Monica
Customer Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Jessica / team —

Thanks — quick note from infra side on sizing and load tests before the kickoff:
- For initial PoC we’ll provision a dedicated instance pool sized to simulate 50 RPS with target p95 < 500ms based on your sample distribution. If the sample shows a spikeier tail we’ll add a transient burst policy.
- We recommend starting with the 8xA100-equivalent profile for the first two weeks to accelerate profiling; we can scale down after tuning if cost becomes a concern.
- Please provide an example payload (1–3 representative requests) so I can sanity-check memory/KV cache usage.

Next meeting: confirmed Tue 2025-05-13 10:00 AM PT — invite sent. I’ll run a 10-minute infra overview and a 15-minute integration demo (Node SDK + export hook).

Vivek
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
